text:
alex: quick share from today's A100/H100 regional sweep — ran fp16 + GPTQ int8 across 13B and 70B variants, measured prefill vs decode, tokens/sec, and normalized $/1M tokens. posting topline and a couple oddities.

priya: love it — did you run with both CUTLASS and Triton kernels? any flash-attention variants?

alex: ran three kernel configs per run: CUTLASS baseline, Triton fused matmuls, and FlashAttention2 for attention ops where supported. command used:```rcli bench --model {model} --gpu {a100|h100} --quant {fp16|int8} --seq 512 --bs 1 --kernels [cutlass,triton,flash2]```

josh: nice. can you drop the numbers? even ballpark is fine.

alex: pasted the compact summary below (all runs single-GPU, 512-token prompt prefill + decode measured; $/1M tokens computed using regional on-demand GPU rates).

alex: Llama-2-13B (512 seq)
- A100 fp16 (CUTLASS): prefill ~450ms, decode ~7.8ms/token, tokens/sec ~128 t/s, $/1M ≈ $1.30
- H100 fp16 (FlashAttention2): prefill ~360ms, decode ~5.6ms/token, tokens/sec ~178 t/s, $/1M ≈ $0.98
- H100 int8 (GPTQ + FlashAttention2): prefill ~340ms, decode ~4.8ms/token, tokens/sec ~208 t/s, $/1M ≈ $0.78

nora: that int8 uplift on H100 is bigger than I expected. stability ok?

alex: yes for 13B. used per-layer clamp + outlier compensation from our quant pipeline, eval on our 2k prompt set showed <0.8% relative drop in top-1 token accuracy.

evan: how about 70B? that's where A100 usually chokes.

alex: Llama-2-70B (512 seq)
- A100 fp16 (CUTLASS): prefill ~1.8s, decode ~32ms/token, tokens/sec ~31 t/s, $/1M ≈ $7.20
- H100 fp16 (Triton + Flash mix): prefill ~1.2s, decode ~18ms/token, tokens/sec ~55 t/s, $/1M ≈ $4.05
- H100 int8 (GPTQ, tuned): prefill ~1.0s, decode ~14ms/token, tokens/sec ~71 t/s, $/1M ≈ $3.20

josh: solid. interesting that Triton+Flash mix helped on H100 for 70B. did you toggle KV cache offload?

alex: yes — for long context (>2k) we tested KV offload to host for A100 (big perf hit) and GPU-resident KV with rotated buffers on H100. Offloading killed decode throughput on A100 (tokens/sec down ~40%).

priya: region differences? eu vs us numbers different?

alex: small but measurable. eu-west1 showed +12-20% higher prefill latency and ~8% lower tokens/sec vs us-west1, mostly due to slightly older instance families in EU we used for parity tests and higher network egress affecting overall RPC loop time. raw GPU compute delta is small; infra (driver/kernel versions) caused most variance.

nora: kernel selection notes? which gave best steady-state tokens/sec?

alex: FlashAttention2 consistently best for attention-heavy parts on H100 — ~10-18% uplift vs Triton for decode on >32k KV cases. CUTLASS still competitive on A100 for fp16 matmuls and needed fewer custom kernels. Triton fused matmuls helped reduce memory copies on H100 and was our go-to for 70B fp16.

evan: any anomalies or regressions?

alex: one oddity: on H100 in eu-west1 we saw a bad driver/kernel combo where int8 inference regressed ~6% in decode speed vs us-west1; a node-level CUDA driver update fixed it. flagged in perf-bot.

perf-bot: automated note — benchmark suite ran 176 jobs, 3 failures (driver mismatch), full logs -> s3://redwood-perf/2026-03-10/1765456789-run.tar.gz :eyes:

josh: what about cost modeling for production autoscale (mix of small/large requests)? any guidance?

alex: quick heuristics we used: for 13B, prefer H100 dedicated pools with int8 profiles for cost-sensitive workloads (≈25–40% cheaper than A100 fp16 at target latency). for 70B, H100 fp16/int8 is the only sane option for sub-2s prefill latencies; A100 reserved capacity only makes sense if you already have commitments or need specific vendor constraints. Also route short-prefill (<128 tokens) to smaller models (7B) to save ~$ per 1M tokens.

priya: thanks! can you drop the raw CSV somewhere? would like to plot region x kernel heatmaps.

alex: uploaded CSV + run scripts to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/bench-1765456789/benchmarks-summary.csv. will follow up with a small notebook for heatmaps tomorrow.

nora: awesome — this helps shape default pool recommendations for Dedicated. :rocket:
